classification.difficultyReason: Substitute signed coefficients into the axis formula, calculate fractional vertex coordinates and use concavity to decide whether x-intercepts exist.

content.prompt: Use the formula $x=\dfrac{-b}{2a}$ to find the axis of symmetry and vertex of the parabolas. Which of them have $x$-intercepts?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-(-1)}{2(1)}\\x&=\frac12\\y&=\left(\frac12\right)^2-\frac12+3\\y&=\frac{11}{4}\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=\dfrac12$ and the vertex is $\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac{11}{4}\right)$. Since the parabola opens upwards, its minimum is $\dfrac{11}{4}>0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-5}{2(3)}\\x&=-\frac56\\y&=3\left(-\frac56\right)^2+5\left(-\frac56\right)-13\\y&=\frac{25}{12}-\frac{50}{12}-\frac{156}{12}\\y&=-\frac{181}{12}\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-\dfrac56$ and the vertex is $\left(-\dfrac56,-\dfrac{181}{12}\right)$. The parabola opens upwards with its minimum below the $x$-axis, so it has two $x$-intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-1}{2(2)}\\x&=-\frac14\\y&=2\left(-\frac14\right)^2-\frac14+1\\y&=\frac78\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-\dfrac14$ and the vertex is $\left(-\dfrac14,\dfrac78\right)$. Since the parabola opens upwards, its minimum is $\dfrac78>0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-3}{2(5)}\\x&=-\frac3{10}\\y&=5\left(-\frac3{10}\right)^2+3\left(-\frac3{10}\right)+7\\y&=\frac9{20}-\frac{18}{20}+\frac{140}{20}\\y&=\frac{131}{20}\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=-\dfrac3{10}$ and the vertex is $\left(-\dfrac3{10},\dfrac{131}{20}\right)$. Since the parabola opens upwards, its minimum is $\dfrac{131}{20}>0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-5}{2(-3)}\\x&=\frac56\\y&=-3\left(\frac56\right)^2+5\left(\frac56\right)-7\\y&=-\frac{25}{12}+\frac{50}{12}-\frac{84}{12}\\y&=-\frac{59}{12}\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=\dfrac56$ and the vertex is $\left(\dfrac56,-\dfrac{59}{12}\right)$. Since the parabola opens downwards, its maximum is $-\dfrac{59}{12}<0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-3}{2(-1)}\\x&=\frac32\\y&=-\left(\frac32\right)^2+3\left(\frac32\right)+2\\y&=\frac{17}{4}\end{align*}$$

The axis is $x=\dfrac32$ and the vertex is $\left(\dfrac32,\dfrac{17}{4}\right)$. The parabola opens downwards with its maximum above the $x$-axis, so it has two $x$-intercepts.
